notes:
Five false statements, found by running Docket's own audit against real sites and checking every finding against the live page.

**A catalogue search reported as a long enquiry form.** `cvr.long_forms` says "for a first contact you usually need a name, one way to reach them, and what they need" and tells the owner to cut fields — but it read a bare count of inputs, which cannot tell a contact form from any other kind. On gutenberg.org that was Project Gutenberg's advanced catalogue search: author, title, subject, LoCC, language, category, filetype. A library cannot shorten its catalogue search to "a name and one way to reach them"; there is nobody to reply to. A form that collects no way to reply is no longer read as an enquiry form.

**Anti-spam honeypots counted as fields the visitor fills in.** The same finding counted nine fields on 170 wpbeginner.com pages. Three are honeypots carrying `tabindex="-1"` and a fourth is a decoy textarea with `aria-hidden="true"`; a reader sees name, email and the comment box. Measured on the real page, the count drops from nine to five. The fields it wanted cut were the spam trap.

**"No Twitter/X card markup" on a site that has it.** The check fires when *more than half* the pages lack a card, then said the site had none. On gutenberg.org, 24 of 44 pages had none — and the other 20, every book page, carry `twitter:card`, `twitter:site`, `twitter:image` and `twitter:image:alt`. It now says how many of how many, and that the rest already have one, because cards on one template and not another is a template to find rather than a site to rebuild.

**Your own subdomain counted as an outbound link.** `links.outbound_quality` opens with the words "A link to your own subdomain is not an outbound link" and filters on it. `links.broken_external`, the function immediately above it, read the same links with no such filter, so gutenberg.org's dead link to `self.gutenberg.org` was one of "4 outbound links are broken", advised as somebody else's page that had moved. It is theirs, and it is down. Own-host breakages are now reported under a title that says so, and both checks answer "is this ours?" from one definition.

**A refused connection from a host that is answering, called a dead sitemap URL.** Two rules shipped a day apart contradicted each other and the suite was not run in between; one of the two controls was red on main. Resolved on the measured evidence: a reset from a host serving other pages says nothing about the URL, and a refusal from a host that answered nothing at all is still reported.

Also verified true, with controls, and left alone: no caching headers, no compression, three genuinely dead third-party links, 44 of 45 pages with no meta description, and two pages sharing one title.
